Theo R: short idea drop-in: perform deterministic body transforms (pii strip, key renames, lightweight normalization) at the edge and make retry ownership explicit via headers. keeps services simpler and centralizes policy.
Priya S: what do we mean by deterministic here? e.g., removing a field is deterministic, but normalizing timestamps might change values depending on timezone if not careful.
Theo R: yeah deterministic = transform outcome only depends on input and policy (no external calls). timezone normalization is fine if we standardize to UTC at edge. non-deterministic enrichments (lookup to HR or KMS) stay downstream.
Jordan: big concern is retries. If gateway mutates and then retries, upstream could see duplicate semantics. we need a reliable handshake so upstreams can detect that edge already applied N transforms.
Nina L: maybe expose a compact transform receipt header with canonical op ids. e.g., `X-RI-TRANSFORM: id=tx-9f8;v=1;ops=drop:cc,rename:acct->account_id` Upstream checks and idempotently ignores re-applying.
Priya S: minor perf note: some customers send massive nested documents. parsing+rewriting could blow p95 latency. can we gate heavy transforms to a side pool?
Theo R: yes two-path approach: inline fast transforms (single-pass streaming drop/rename) vs worker-pool where WASM/JS transforms run off-path. if pool saturated, edge will pass through and emit `X-RI-TRANSFORM-SKIP: reason=overload`.
ops-bot: rolling canary: edge-transformations/2026-04-02 queued for canary at 03:00 UTC.
Jordan: routing/retry ownership: propose gateway owns transport-level retries (connect timeout, EOF) and will only retry idempotent methods by default. application retries (retrying POST semantics) remain with the upstream if it has domain knowledge. we signal boundary with `X-RI-RETRY-OWNER: gateway|upstream`.
Nina L: if gateway retries and upstream might have side effects, we should require `Idempotency-Key` or else use confirm-on-retry semantics (first retry does a lightweight probe e.g., HEAD).
Priya S: rollout plan suggestion: 1) enable drop-only sanitizers on non-prod zones, 2) preview flag in prod where edge returns `X-RI-TRANSFORM-PREVIEW` with a small JSON diff but doesn't apply, 3) enable rename ops for low-traffic routes, 4) flip transform-on for pinned services.
Theo R: preview header format idea: base64 small JSON diff or simple ops list. keep header under 2KB. also stream-transform metrics to tracer: op latency, bytes scanned, ops count.
Jordan: observability: add transform span with op names and include in Console breadcrumbs. make ops searchable in logs for debugging incidents where transforms cause 4xx.
Nina L: security: Private deploys may forbid certain transforms that touch secrets or call KMS. catalog flags should honor deployment type.
Priya S: versioning: every transform policy needs a version token. `v=1` in header. upgrades should be backward-compatible or config must pin older v for services that rely on previous behavior.
ops-bot: note: please file RFC-PR referencing this thread under /rfc/edge-transforms with runbook items.
Theo R: implementation notes for runtime team: small streaming lexer for JSON path ops, sandbox WASM for heavier rules, per-route config resolved via catalog cache, header emission/parsing, preview endpoint, circuit breaker for transform worker pool.
Jordan: default failure mode = passthrough + emit metric + 1x log. avoid failing user request because transform engine choked.
Nina L: agreed. I'll draft RFC covering headers, retry ownership, catalog flags, preview behaviors, rollout steps, and test checklist. tagging eng-runtime & infra.
Theo R: awesome. thanks all :party_parrot:
